question_stem:
A cell of electromotive force (e.m.f.) 0.48 V is connected to a metal wire X, as shown in Fig. 6.1.
The cell has internal resistance. The current in the cell is 0.80 A.
Wire X has length 3.0 m, cross-sectional area 1.3 × 10^{-7} m^{2} and resistance 0.40 Ω.
question_stem_latex:
A cell of electromotive force (e.m.f.) 0.48 V is connected to a metal wire X, as shown in Fig. 6.1.
The cell has internal resistance. The current in the cell is 0.80 A.
Wire X has length 3.0 m, cross-sectional area $1.3 \times 10^{-7}\,\mathrm{m}^{2}$ and resistance 0.40 $\Omega$.

parts.label: (a)
parts.question_text:
Calculate the charge passing through the cell in a time of 7.5 minutes.
charge = C

$charge = C $

parts.label: (b)
parts.question_text:
Calculate the percentage efficiency with which the cell supplies power to wire X.
efficiency = %
parts.question_text_latex:
Calculate the percentage efficiency with which the cell supplies power to wire X.
$efficiency = % $

parts.label: (c)
parts.question_text:
There are 3.2 × 10^{22} free (conduction) electrons contained in the volume of wire X.
For wire X, calculate:

For wire X, calculate:

parts.question_text:
the number density n of the free electrons
n = m^{-3}

the number density n of the free electrons
$n = m^{-3} $

parts.label: (c)(ii)
parts.question_text:
the average drift speed of the free electrons.
average drift speed = m s^{-1}
parts.question_text_latex:
the average drift speed of the free electrons.
$average drift speed = m s^{-1} $

parts.label: (d)
parts.question_text:
A wire Y has the same cross-sectional area as wire X and is made of the same metal. Wire Y
is longer than wire X.
Wire X in the circuit is now replaced by wire Y. Assume that wire Y has the same temperature
as wire X.
State and explain whether the average drift speed of the free electrons in wire Y is greater
than, the same as, or less than that in wire X.
